sections.heading: PUGET SOUND NEARSHORE ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, WASHINGTON
sections.title: III
sections.own_text: In carrying out the project for ecosystem restoration, Puget Sound, Washington, authorized by section 1401(4) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2016 (130 Stat. 1713; 136 Stat. 3806), the Secretary shall consider the removal, relocation, and replacement of the following sites to be a project feature the costs of which are shared as construction:

children.own_text: Highway 101 causeway and bridge over the Lilliwaup Estuary of the Hood Canal site.
NE North Shore Road roadway and bridge over the Tahuya Estuary of the Hood Canal site.
Highway 101 causeway and bridge over the Snow Creek and Salmon Creek (at the head of Discovery Bay) site.
County and local roads and bridges over the Nooksack and Lummi Rivers and Tennant Creek at the Nooksack Estuary of the Northern Puget Sound site.

sections.label: SEC. 345.
sections.heading: WASHINGTON METROPOLITAN AREA, WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, MARYLAND, AND VIRGINIA
sections.title: III

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: In carrying out the feasibility study for the project for water supply, Washington, District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia, authorized by section 8201(a)(14) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2022 (136 Stat. 3745; 138 Stat. 3160), the Secretary shall carry out a second phase of the study focused on the identification of a secondary water source and additional water storage capability or other long-term and large-scale backup water supply solutions necessary to meaningfully reduce the structural water supply risk of the region.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Treatment of Study
children.own_text: In carrying out the second phase of the study under this section, the Secretary--
shall treat such study as a continuation of the first phase of the study carried out under section 8201(a)(14) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2022; and
shall continue such study without a new investment decision.

sections.label: SEC. 346.
sections.heading: FEDERAL TRIANGLE AREA, WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA
sections.title: III

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: In carrying out an analysis of a measure benefitting Federal land under the administrative jurisdiction of the head of another Federal agency as part of the feasibility study for the project for flood risk management, Federal Triangle Area, Washington, District of Columbia, authorized by section 8201(a)(12) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2022 (136 Stat. 3745), the Secretary may use, for any portion of the cost of such analysis, funds--
made available to the Secretary for water resources development investigations; or
contributed by such agency head.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Federal Expense Requirement
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out each analysis described in subsection (a) at Federal expense.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Savings Provision
children.own_text: Nothing in this section affects any cost- sharing requirement applicable to the head of a Federal agency, other than the Secretary, for the construction of an authorized water resources development project, or a separable element of such project, resulting from the study described in subsection (a).

sections.label: SEC. 502.
sections.heading: STUDY ON HIGH HAZARD POTENTIAL DAM PRIORITIZATIONS
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency shall complete a study to identify the issues and concerns that prevent States from prioritizing projects that will have the greatest community benefit under section 8A of the National Dam Safety Program Act (33 U.S.C. 467f-2) and produce recommendations on how to address such issues and concerns.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Timeline
children.own_text: The Administrator shall begin the study required under subsection (a) on the date of enactment of this Act and shall submit to Congress a status report on such study not later than 1 year after such date of enactment.
